newsitem.title: USA: Prize winning author and astronomer Carl Sagan dies.
newsitem.headline: Prize winning author and astronomer Carl Sagan dies.

text.p: Astronomer and Pulitzer Prize-winning author Carl Sagan, who spent his life investigating the possiblity of life in outer space, died on Friday at age 62, a cancer centre spokeswoman said.
Sagan died from pneumonia after a suffering from a bone marrow disease for two years, Susan Edmonds, spokeswoman for the Fred Hutchinson Cancer Research Centre said.

Sagan won the Pulitzer in 1978 for his book "Dragons of Eden" and was the author of several other best-selling books on space and the universe, including "Intelligent Life in the Universe," "Mars and the Mind of Man," and "Other Worlds."

He was a professor at Cornell University, the Director of the Laboratory for Planetary Studies, and a pioneer in the field of exobiology, the branch of biology investigating the possibility of extraterrestial life.
He appeared on several television shows, including the BBC production "The Violent Planet" and the PBS show "Cosmos," which he produduced beginning in 1977.
He was diagnosed with the fatal bone marrow cancer in 1994 and had an up-and-down battle with the disease.
He was noted educator who lectured astronauts, college students and Air Force Acedemy classes. He won dozens of awards for his ability to translate universal concepts into ordinary language.
